Optimal.Notes: A slight render resolution reduction with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU comfortable while hitting the 60 fps target the game was designed for. High textures preserve visual fidelity where it matters most.

profiles.Summary: Dark Souls Remastered runs well on the Steam Deck, benefiting from its relatively modest PC requirements and native 60 fps target — the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably meets the recommended spec. ProtonDB reports a platinum rating with strong confidence, indicating most players experience a smooth, near-issue-free experience out of the box.
profiles.BasisNote: Profiles are based on the strong platinum ProtonDB rating (418 reports, 0.87 score) indicating excellent overall compatibility, combined with the game's modest PC requirements relative to Deck hardware; no specific Deck settings guides were available, so in-game option names follow standard FromSoftware DSR settings — verify option names on first launch and watch frame rate in Blighttown or Izalith, which are historically the most demanding areas.

MaxBattery.Notes: Locked to 30 fps with a low TDP and reduced render resolution upscaled via FSR to stretch battery life as far as possible. The game is very playable at 30 fps given its deliberate combat pacing.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full native resolution at max settings; the Deck's GPU exceeds the recommended spec for this title and can sustain 60 fps in most areas. Motion blur is left off as it adds little value at 60 fps and can obscure combat reads.

Optimal.Notes: Rendering at 1152x720 with mild FSR upscaling delivers a sharp, stable 60 fps experience that looks close to native on the 1280x800 OLED panel. This is the recommended sweet spot given the game's modest PC requirements relative to the Deck's GPU.

profiles.Summary: Dark Souls Remastered runs very well on the Steam Deck, with its modest PC requirements (GTX 660 recommended) sitting comfortably within the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capabilities, allowing a stable 60 fps at native resolution. ProtonDB rates it platinum with strong confidence, and the game's built-in 60 fps hard cap means the Deck can hit the maximum frame rate without issue at medium-to-high settings.
profiles.BasisNote: Profiles are based on ProtonDB's platinum rating with 418 reports and strong confidence trend, combined with the game's PC requirements relative to the Deck's GPU; no specific Deck settings guides were found, so in-game option names are inferred from the remaster's PC settings menu — verify option names on first launch.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 and a 6 W TDP cap dramatically extends battery life while keeping the game fully playable. Half-rate shading is left off as it can introduce visual artifacts with this game's lighting model.

KnownIssues: Online multiplayer (invasions, co-op) may be unreliable or non-functional under Proton due to EasyAntiCheat; offline play is fully stable
The game engine hard-caps at 60 fps, so the OLED's 90 Hz refresh rate offers no frame rate benefit beyond 60
Some players report occasional stuttering in particle-heavy areas such as Blighttown under Proton
Controller button prompts may default to Xbox layout rather than Steam Deck layout, which is cosmetic only

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably handles native 1280x800 at high settings, keeping a near-locked 60 fps in most areas; minor dips may occur in dense particle-effect zones like Blighttown. The game's 60 fps engine cap is the ceiling regardless of hardware headroom.
